output.title: Spot duplicate emails before they turn into cleanup
output.body:
If you run a small business, the real question is not whether duplicate emails exist. It is whether they reach you before you act on them. That is the bounded workflow decision: do duplicates get caught early enough to prevent inconsistent replies, extra review, or manual cleanup later?

Start by looking at three recent examples from your own inbox or CRM. For each one, ask where it came from: the same person wrote twice, two systems created the same contact, or you copied the thread into another tool. Then decide which duplicates must be caught before action and which can be cleaned up after. An invoice or payment request belongs in the first group; a newsletter usually does not. Human approval stays in place for anything involving money or other high-risk decisions.

The next practical step is a one-week manual test. Put suspicious duplicates into one folder and review them by hand. Count only three things: real duplicates, false positives, and the time your review takes. That gives you a simple answer to whether the problem is worth a later workflow change. If the definition is messy, that is still useful. It means the first fix is clearer rules, not a bigger tool. Small problem, small test, no theatre.
